mainTopic: קנין אגב: must the movable items be piled on the land being acquired (צבורים)?
overview: The גמרא asks whether, in a קנין אגב (acquiring movables along with land), the movable items must physically sit on the land (צבורים). First it tests a משנה that says even a tiny plot can carry movables. רב שמואל בר ביסנא answers that a needle could be stuck in the plot. רב יוסף objects, and רב אשי defends the answer: a valuable pearl could hang on the needle. Next, רבי אלעזר tells of a man from Madon (מדוני) who gave away a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels by means of a בית סלע. The גמרא answers that a בית סלע was really a big, rock-hard field. Then רב יהודה, quoting רב, tells of a man who gave a טפח by טפח of land together with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels. The גמרא answers that he was giving their value in money. It then works through why he needed land at all: the recipient was not there, and the giver did not trust a middleman. None of these sources settles the question, and the amud ends as the גמרא begins a new proof from רבן גמליאל and the זקנים on a ship.

steps.title: Proof from a tiny plot of land
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says even a tiny plot of land can be used to acquire movables along with it. If the movables had to be piled on the land, what could a tiny plot hold?
steps.simpleTranslation: Land of any size can be used to write a פרוסבול and to acquire movable property along with it. If you say the movables must be piled on the land, what is a tiny plot good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about land of any size. It then uses that משנה to argue that movables do not need to sit on the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a plot of any size works for קנין אגב. A tiny plot cannot hold much of anything. So, the argument goes, the movables must not need to be piled on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A court document that keeps a loan from being cancelled by שמיטה
Movable property (things a lender cannot collect from once they are sold)
Piled up; the movables physically sitting on the land
Any amount at all, even the tiniest

phrases.english: and one can write a prosbol based on it,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a משנה in מסכת פאה that started just before: even the tiniest piece of land counts for these laws.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִקְנוֹת עִמָּהּ נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת.
phrases.english: and one can acquire movable property along with it.
And if you say we require the movables to be piled on it,
what is a tiny plot of land good for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים, כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לְמַאי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof the גמרא began just before this section, quoting the end of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That movables do not need to be piled on the land in קנין אגב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that land of any size can be used to acquire movables

steps.title: A needle stuck in the tiny plot
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר ביסנא explains the משנה as a case where a needle was stuck into the tiny plot. So even a tiny plot can hold something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר ביסנא explained it in front of רב יוסף: for example, where he stuck a needle into the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר ביסנא pushes back on the proof. He shows that a tiny plot can still hold a small item, like a needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed a tiny plot holds nothing at all. A needle can sit in even the smallest piece of land. So the משנה still fits the view that the items must be on the land.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Bisna explained it
before Rav Yosef:
For example, where he stuck a needle into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּומַאּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בִּיסְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by giving a case where a tiny plot holds something.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows that the משנה does not prove anything
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a tiny plot can hold nothing, but a needle fits.

steps.title: רב יוסף: would the תנא bother about a needle?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף strongly objects. A תנא would not go to the trouble of teaching a law just for something as small as a needle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: You disgust me! Did the תנא bother to teach us about a needle?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב שמואל בר ביסנא's explanation as too unlikely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says a needle is too unimportant a case. The משנה would not list a law just for it. So the needle answer does not really explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה or משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him: You disgust me!
Did the tanna go to the trouble to teach us about a needle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the needle explanation from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר ביסנא's needle explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A needle is too trivial for the תנא to teach a law about.

steps.title: רב אשי: a valuable pearl on the needle
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי defends the needle explanation. A pearl worth a thousand זוז might be hanging on the needle, so the case is worth teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Who says he did not hang a pearl worth a thousand זוז on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רב יוסף's objection and saves the needle explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said a needle is too small to matter. רב אשי answers that something very valuable could hang from it. So the needle case is worth teaching, and the original proof stays rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about a tiny plot does not decide whether the items must be piled on the land. A needle, even one holding a precious pearl, can sit on the smallest plot.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאן לֵימָא לַן
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Who says to us
that he did not hang a pearl on it
worth a thousand zuz?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאן לֵימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case so it is significant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A needle alone is too trivial to be the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A needle holding a costly pearl is an important case, so the משנה can be talking about it.

steps.title: The story of the Madonite's gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר tells of a man from Madon who gave away many movables by means of a בית סלע near ירושלים, and the חכמים upheld his gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: רבי אלעזר said, there was a story of a Madonite in ירושלים who had many movables and wanted to give them as a gift. They told him the only way was to transfer them by means of land. He acquired a בית סלע near ירושלים and said: this northern part goes to so-and-so, and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels. He died, and they carried out his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the question. This step tells the story; the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that a huge amount of property, a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, was transferred through a בית סלע. The name sounds like a plot the size of a coin. The חכמים still upheld the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy, a way to do it

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Elazar said:
There was an incident with a certain Madonite who was in Jerusalem
who had a great deal of movable property,
and he wanted to give it away as a gift.
They said to him: There is no remedy
unless he transfers them by means of land.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה? הָלַךְ וְלָקַח בֵּית סֶלַע
phrases.english: What did he do? He went and acquired a beit sela
phrases.notes: The name sounds like a plot the size of a סלע coin. That is exactly what the next step will argue.

phrases.english: near Jerusalem, and said:
"This northern part is for so-and-so,
and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels,"
and he died, and they carried out his words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, the גמרא brings a new source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That movables do not need to be piled on the land in קנין אגב
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's story of the Madonite and the בית סלע

steps.title: A tiny plot cannot hold a hundred sheep
steps.stepSummary: If the movables had to be piled on the land, how could a coin-sized plot hold a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we require the movables to be piled on it, what is a בית סלע good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plot the size of a coin could never hold a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels. Yet the gift was upheld. That suggests the movables do not need to sit on the land.

phrases.english: And if you say we require the movables to be piled on it,
what is a beit sela good for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בָּעֵינַן צְבוּרִים בָּהּ, בֵּית סֶלַע לְמַאי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the story in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That movables need not be piled on the land
steps.raayaSupportSource: A coin-sized plot could not hold all the gifts, yet the gift worked.

steps.title: A בית סלע was really a big field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A בית סלע was not coin-sized; it was a very large plot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think a בית סלע means literally the size of a סלע coin? What does סלע mean here? A plot that is very large.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by rereading the term בית סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the plot being tiny. If the plot was large, the sheep and barrels could really have been on it. So the story proves nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read בית סלע as 'a plot the size of a coin' here. The גמרא concludes it means a large, rocky field.

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ בֵּית סֶלַע, סֶלַע מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: Do you think a beit sela means literally the size of a sela?
What is "sela"? A place that is very large.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ בֵּית סֶלַע, סֶלַע מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 6 by rereading the term.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the Madonite story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed בית סלע means a coin-sized plot.

steps.title: Why call a big field סלע?
steps.stepSummary: If the plot was large, the גמרא asks why it was called a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call it סלע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the name, setting up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סלע seemed to point to a coin-sized plot. If the field was large, the name needs another explanation.

phrases.english: And why did they call it sela?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name, following the rereading in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a large field would be called סלע

steps.title: Because it was hard as rock
steps.stepSummary: It was called סלע because the ground was hard like rock, not because it was small.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was hard like a rock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the name, and that finishes the rejection of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סלע also means 'rock.' The field got its name from its hard, rocky ground, not its size. So the story does not prove that movables need not be piled on the land, and the question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: Neither the משנה about a tiny plot nor the Madonite story proves anything. The question of whether movables must be צבורים on the land is still unresolved.

phrases.english: Because it was hard as a rock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name סלע describes the rock-hard ground, not a small size.

steps.title: A man gives a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels with a tiny piece of land
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב about a man who bought a בית רובע plot near ירושלים. He gave one טפח by טפח of it to someone, together with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, and the חכמים upheld the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A man got sick in ירושלים (this fits רבי אליעזר; others say he was healthy, which fits רבנן). He had many movables and wanted to give them as a gift. They told him the only way was to transfer them along with land. So he bought a בית רובע near ירושלים and said: 'A טפח by a טפח goes to so-and-so, and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.' He died, and the חכמים upheld his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story as another proof about giving movables along with land. This step only tells the story. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows a gift of many movables tied to a tiny piece of land, one טפח by one טפח. The detail about sick or healthy explains why he needed a real קנין at all. According to רבי אליעזר even a sick man needs a real קנין, and according to רבנן only a healthy man does.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
Along with land (transferring movables together with land)
A small plot of land, the size needed to plant a quarter-measure of seed
A handbreadth, about the width of four fingers

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
There was an incident with a certain man who became sick in Jerusalem
according to Rabbi Eliezer;
phrases.notes: Calling him sick fits רבי אליעזר, who says even a dying man needs a real קנין to give things away.

phrases.english: and some say: he was healthy, according to the Rabbis,
who had a lot of movable property
and wanted to give it as a gift.
They said to him: there is no way for him
except to transfer them along with land.
What did he do? He went and acquired
a beit rova of land near Jerusalem,
and said: "A handbreadth by a handbreadth to so-and-so,
and with it a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels,"
and he died, and the Sages upheld his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the בית סלע story (steps 5-9) was pushed off, the גמרא brings another story as a new proof on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That movables given along with land do not need to be piled on the land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the story of the man who gave a טפח by טפח with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.

steps.title: A tiny piece of land cannot hold all those animals and barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the proof: if the movables had to be piled on the land, one טפח by one טפח could never hold them, yet the gift worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the movables must be piled on the land, what is a טפח by a טפח good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out why the story is a proof. A tiny square of land cannot hold a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, so they must not need to be piled on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same logic as the בית סלע proof in step 6, now applied to an even smaller piece of land. Since the חכמים upheld the gift, it seems piling the movables on the land is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Piled up (the movables sitting on the land)
What is it good for? (what can it hold?)

phrases.english: And if you say we require the movables to be piled on it,
what is a handbreadth by a handbreadth fit for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the story told in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: Piling the movables on the land is not required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tiny טפח by טפח could not physically hold a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, yet the gift was upheld.

steps.title: He was giving money, not actual sheep and barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the story is about money, meaning the value of the sheep and barrels, and coins can fit on a small piece of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the story differently. He was giving the cash value of the sheep and barrels, not the animals themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he gave coins, they could fit on a טפח by טפח. So the story no longer shows that piling is unnecessary, because the gift may have been piled on the land after all.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (the גמרא limits the case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With money.
phrases.notes: He means the value of a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, in coins that can fit on a small square of land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11 by redefining what was given.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the tiny piece of land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed real sheep and barrels, but the gift may have been their value in money, which fits on a טפח.

steps.title: Support for the money reading: real animals could have been given with חליפין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the money reading. If he were giving actual sheep and barrels, he could have used חליפין and would not have needed land at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense, because if you think it was actual sheep and barrels, let him transfer them to the recipient through חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a reason why the 'money' reading is likely correct. Buying land only makes sense if no easier קנין was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Actual animals and barrels can be acquired through חליפין, which is easy. Money cannot be acquired through חליפין. Since he went to the trouble of buying land, it seems he was giving money.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense: the גמרא supports the last answer
It enters your mind, you might think
A קנין by exchange, usually handing over a cloth or object

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if it enters your mind
that it was actual hundred sheep and hundred barrels,
let him transfer them to him through symbolic exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the money reading from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the story was about money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Real sheep and barrels could have been given through חליפין, so using land points to money.

steps.title: But money could have been given with משיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the support: even if it was money, he could have used משיכה and still would not have needed land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what, it was money? Let him transfer it to the recipient through משיכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reasoning of step 13. Money also had an easier way to be transferred, so the land does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that land was used because no easier קנין existed. But money can be acquired by משיכה, pulling it. So the 'why use land?' question applies to money too.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather what? (turning the question back)
A קנין by pulling the object toward oneself

phrases.english: But rather, what? It was money?
Let him transfer it to him by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the supporting argument of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument that using land proves the gift was money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money also has an easy קנין, משיכה, so the argument 'he would have used an easier קנין' proves nothing about money versus sheep.

steps.title: The real reason for land: the recipient was not there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says we are forced to explain that the person getting the gift was not present, so משיכה was impossible and land was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the recipient of the gift was not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the משיכה question. He used land because the receiver was absent and could not pull anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משיכה needs the receiver to do the pulling himself. If he was not there, giving it along with land was the only option. This gives a new reason for using land that has nothing to do with money.

phrases.english: Rather: the recipient of the gift was not present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the recipient was absent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Money could have been given with משיכה, so why land?
steps.terutzMaskana: The receiver was not there to pull, so land was the only way.

steps.title: The same answer works for real sheep, so the support falls away
steps.stepSummary: If the recipient was absent, חליפין would not work for real sheep either, so the support for the money reading collapses.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, the recipient of the gift was not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back on step 13. The absent receiver explains using land even for real sheep and barrels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליפין also needs the receiver present, so an absent receiver explains the land in the sheep case too. That means using land does not prove the gift was money. The money reading from step 12 can still stand as a possible answer, but it has lost its extra support.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, the same applies here

steps.whatToRemember: The second proof was pushed off by saying he gave money. The attempt to prove that reading failed, because an absent receiver explains why land was used either way.

phrases.english: So too, the recipient of the gift was not present.
phrases.notes: Read it as: even with real sheep, he couldn't use חליפין because the receiver wasn't there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 15 to cancel the support brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the support for the money reading (step 13), not the money reading itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An absent receiver explains using land in the sheep case too, so using land does not prove the gift was money.

steps.title: Why not transfer it through another person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the recipient was not there, the giver could have had a third party acquire the items for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him transfer them to him through another person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that land was the only option. It points out that a third person could have taken hold of the items on behalf of the absent recipient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said land was needed because the recipient was not there to do משיכה. But a person can acquire something for someone else (זכייה), so someone else could have done משיכה for him. If that works, land was not truly necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let him transfer them by having someone acquire them on the recipient's behalf
acquiring something for another person, even when that person is not present
through another person (here, a third party)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אַגַּב here does not mean the קנין אגב of land. It just means 'through' another person who acts as a middleman.

phrases.english: But let him transfer them to him through another person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from step 15 that land was the only way to complete the gift for an absent recipient.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that land was required because the recipient was absent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third party can acquire on the absent recipient's behalf through משיכה, so land was not the only option.

steps.title: He did not trust a middleman
steps.stepSummary: The giver did not want to rely on a third party. He worried the person would grab the items and use them himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not trust that option. He thought the middleman might grab them and use them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the giver chose not to use a third party because he was afraid that person would keep the items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The option existed by law, but the giver did not trust it in practice. So land was his only option that he felt safe with, and the story still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not rely on it; he was not comfortable with it
grabs and consumes (takes the items for himself)

phrases.english: He did not rely on that,
he thought: he will grab them and use them up.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the middleman. The giver feared he would keep the items instead of passing them on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason: the option existed but the giver chose not to trust it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using a third party was easy, so land was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The giver did not trust a middleman, so he used land instead.

steps.title: Then why say 'he has no remedy'?
steps.stepSummary: If a third party was really possible, why did the earlier statement say he had 'no remedy' except land?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'he has no remedy' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. The earlier statement sounded like land was the only possible way, yet we just said another way existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אין לו תקנה' mean there is no other way at all. But step 18 admitted a legal option existed and he simply did not trust it. So the wording seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: if so, what then (introduces a challenge)
he has no remedy; there is no other way

phrases.english: If so, what is meant by "he has no remedy"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18 using the wording of the original statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a third party was possible but not trusted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'No remedy' means no other legal way, but step 18 admits one existed.

steps.title: No remedy, given that he did not trust a middleman
steps.stepSummary: The statement means: since he would not rely on a third party, his only remaining option was to transfer through land.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: since he did not trust a middleman, he had no remedy except to transfer them through land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads 'no remedy' as true only from the giver's point of view. Since he refused to use a middleman, land was his only choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No remedy' is not a general legal rule. It describes this giver, who had already ruled out a third party. So the story proves nothing either way about קנין אגב when the items are not lying on the land, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: by means of land (through a land transfer)

steps.whatToRemember: The story about the gift through land gives no clear proof. 'He has no remedy' only means that, since he would not trust a middleman, land was his only choice.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
since he did not rely on a middleman,
he has no remedy
unless he transfers them by means of land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by explaining the wording 'no remedy'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: 'no remedy' applies only within the giver's own choice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No remedy' means land was the only legal method.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means land was his only option once he refused to trust a middleman, so the story proves nothing about קנין אגב.

steps.title: New proof: רבן גמליאל on the ship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new proof from a story about רבן גמליאל and the זקנים traveling on a ship, where he gave away מעשר he had not yet separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was a story with רבן גמליאל and the זקנים, who were traveling on a ship. רבן גמליאל said to the זקנים: The tenth that I will measure out in the future...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof. It starts quoting a story about רבן גמליאל on a ship, and the story continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last proof fell apart, so the גמרא tries again. In this story רבן גמליאל was far from his produce yet still gave away his מעשר. The rest of the story will show how he did it, and that is what may teach us about קנין אגב.

keyTerms.meaning: one-tenth; the tithe (מעשר) taken from produce

phrases.english: Come and hear:

who were traveling on a ship,

steps.raayaObject: Whether movable items can be acquired through land when they are not lying on that land.
